source_text: Respondi ergo ibi: Tu quidem (pace magisterii tui dixerim) tergiversaris, sed intellege quod ademerit tibi veritas licentiam pervagandi. Ecce enim et nos acquiescimus, quia peccatum opus est malae voluntatis, vel opus est diaboli; sed per quid hoc peccatum invenitur in parvulo? Per voluntatem? At nulla in eo fuit. Per formam corporis? Sed hanc Deus tribuit. Per ingressum animae? Sed nihil debet semini corporali, quae nova a Deo conditur. Per nuptias? Sed hae pertinent ad opus parentum, quos in hoc actu non peccasse praemiseras; quod si non vere id concesseras, sicut processus tui sermonis indicat, ipsae sunt exsecrandae, quae causam fecerunt mali. Verum illae substantiam propriam non habent; sed nomine suo personarum opus indicant; parentes igitur, qui conventu suo causam fecere peccato, iure damnabiles. Ambigi ergo iam non potest, coniuges aeterno supplicio mancipari, quorum labore actum est, ut ad dominatum exercendum in homines diabolus perveniret. Quod si concesseris; illud totum quod antea tenuisse videbaris, amittes, id est, quod hominem Dei opus dixeras. Necessario quippe sequitur, quia per commixtionem corporum origo progenitis est, si per originem malum in hominibus, per malum ius diaboli in homines, diabolum esse auctorem hominum, a quo est origo nascentium [n24] . Post quae ipsius denuo verba repetivi: Nam sicut peccatum, sive hinc, sive inde trahatur, opus est diaboli; sic homo, sive hinc, sive inde nascatur, opus est Dei. Ac protinus insurrexi hoc modo: Cum illam vocem timoris tui cogito, qua dicis nuptias malum non esse, istos alios sermones tuos sine risu considerare non possum. Si enim credis a Deo homines fieri, et esse coniuges innocentes, vide quam stare non possit, trahi ex his originale peccatum. Certe non peccat iste qui nascitur, non peccat ille qui genuit, non peccat ille qui condidit; per quas rimas, inter tot praesidia innocentiae, peccatum fingis ingressum?
pass_a_gloss: I answered therefore there: You indeed (let me have said it with peace of your teaching-office) are shifting, but understand that the truth has taken from you the license of wandering. For look, we too acquiesce, because sin is a work of an evil will, or is a work of the devil; but through what is this sin found in a little child? Through will? But there was none in him. Through the form of the body? But God bestowed this. Through the entrance of the soul? But it owes nothing to bodily seed, which is founded new by God. Through marriages? But these belong to the work of the parents, whom you had sent ahead as not having sinned in this act; which if you had not truly granted, as the progress of your speech indicates, they themselves are to be execrated, who made the cause of the evil. But they do not have a substance of their own; but by their name they indicate the work of persons; the parents therefore, who by their coming-together made a cause for sin, are justly damnable. It can therefore now not be doubted that spouses are made over to eternal punishment, by whose labor it was brought about that the devil arrived at exercising dominion over human beings. Which if you shall have granted, you will lose that whole which you previously seemed to have held, that is, that you had said a human being is a work of God. For it necessarily follows, because through the mingling of bodies there is an origin for those begotten, if through origin an evil in human beings, through evil a right of the devil over human beings, that the devil is the author of human beings, from whom is the origin of those being born. After which I repeated his words again: For just as sin, whether it is drawn from here or from there, is a work of the devil; so a human being, whether he is born from here or from there, is a work of God. And at once I rose up in this way: When I think of that voice of your fear, by which you say that marriages are not an evil, I cannot consider these other speeches of yours without laughter. For if you believe that human beings are made by God, and that spouses are innocent, see how it cannot stand that original sin is drawn from these. Certainly this one who is born does not sin, that one who begot does not sin, that one who founded does not sin; through what cracks, among so many guards of innocence, do you invent sin to have entered?

pass_b_english: There I replied: ‘With due respect to your teaching authority, you are evading the issue. But understand that the truth has taken away your freedom to wander. Look: we too agree that sin is the work of an evil will, or the devil’s work. But through what is this sin found in an infant? Through the will? Yet there has been no will in the infant. Through the body’s form? But God gave that. Through the soul’s arrival? But the soul, newly created by God, owes nothing to bodily seed. Through marriage? But marriage belongs to the parents’ activity, and you previously said that they did not sin in this act. If that concession was insincere, as your subsequent argument indicates, marriage itself must be cursed for causing the evil. Yet marriage has no substance of its own: its name designates people’s activity. The parents, then, whose union caused sin, rightly deserve condemnation. There can therefore no longer be any doubt that married people are consigned to eternal punishment, since their activity enabled the devil to gain dominion over human beings. If you concede this, you lose everything you previously seemed to maintain: namely, your statement that a human being is God’s work. For the offspring’s origin lies in the union of bodies. Therefore, if evil comes into human beings through their origin, and the devil’s right over human beings comes through evil, it necessarily follows that the devil is the maker of human beings, since the origin of those born comes from him’ (quoted in Augustine, Marriage and Desire 2.44–49). After this I repeated his words: ‘For just as sin, whether derived from this source or that, is the devil’s work, so a human being, whether born from this source or that, is God’s work.’ At once I challenged him as follows: ‘When I think of that frightened statement of yours that marriage is not evil, I cannot consider these other remarks without laughing. If you believe that human beings are made by God and that married people are innocent, see how impossible it is to maintain that original sin is derived from them. Certainly the one born does not sin, the one who fathered the child does not sin, and the one who created the child does not sin. Through what cracks, amid so many defenses of innocence, do you imagine sin has entered?’

Parents insofar as parents are not guilty; keep the forensic 'in quantum parentes sunt'.
